over-time.title: How old the living are
over-time.caption: After every game of the 30 worlds. Left: the median age of the agents alive, and the age that nine in ten of them are below (the 90th percentile). Right: the age of the oldest agent alive; the dashed diagonal is the age of an agent alive since iteration 0, which only the oldest can follow. For each, the line is the median of the worlds at each iteration, the darker band holds the middle half of them (from the 25th to the 75th percentile) and the paler band nine in ten (5th to 95th).
over-time.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames after every game (frame `2·t + 1`, `gol_store.read_frame`), read in order by `book_chapters.ages.lifelines`: every agent's `ages` entry gives its birth iteration (the frame's iteration minus its age), and the last frame it is in its last iteration alive.

1. After every game, the median, the 90th percentile and the largest of `ages`.
2. Cut the 1,500 iterations into 600 stretches of 2.5 and take each world's mean in each stretch.
3. In each stretch, take the median, the 25th and 75th and the 5th and 95th percentiles of those means over the worlds that still have a value there (a world that died has none after its death).

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py ages`.

pyramids.title: The living, by age, at six moments
pyramids.caption: All agents alive after the games of 100, 250, 500, 750, 1,000 and 1,475, pooled over the 30 worlds and sorted by age in classes that widen fourfold: born in that very iteration (age 0), 1 to 3, 4 to 15, 16 to 63, 64 to 255, and 256 iterations or more. Each column adds up to 1.
pyramids.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames after every game (frame `2·t + 1`, `gol_store.read_frame`), read in order by `book_chapters.ages.lifelines`: every agent's `ages` entry gives its birth iteration (the frame's iteration minus its age), and the last frame it is in its last iteration alive.

1. Every 25 iterations, count the agents of each age class; pool the worlds.
2. Divide each class by the agents of the moment and stack.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py ages`.

cohorts.title: How long agents live, by when they were born
cohorts.caption: Of all agents born in each period of the 30 worlds' lives that were alive after at least one game, the share that lived at least L iterations. A life is counted from the iteration of birth to the last iteration after whose game the agent was alive, both included; lives still going at the end of a run are counted as far as they went (Kaplan–Meier, as in [Births, deaths and ages](births-deaths-and-ages.md)). A period's line stops at the longest life its agents could have had before the run ended. Both axes logarithmic.
cohorts.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames after every game (frame `2·t + 1`, `gol_store.read_frame`), read in order by `book_chapters.ages.lifelines`: every agent's `ages` entry gives its birth iteration (the frame's iteration minus its age), and the last frame it is in its last iteration alive.

1. For every agent, its birth iteration b and its last iteration alive d; d − b + 1 iterations lived; alive after the run's last game: still going.
2. Sort the agents by b into the periods shown, pool the worlds, and estimate S(L) by Kaplan–Meier (`book_chapters.ages.survival`).

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py ages`.

expectancy.title: Life expectancy over a world's life
expectancy.caption: Agents born in each stretch of 25 iterations (those born at iteration 0, the founders and their first children, left out). Left: how many of their first 100 iterations they live on average — the sum of the Kaplan–Meier curve up to L = 100, a mean that every stretch born at least 100 iterations before the end can be measured by in full. Right: the median lifetime, the longest L that more than half of them live. For each world separately; the line is the median of the 30 worlds, the darker band the middle half and the paler band nine in ten.
expectancy.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames after every game (frame `2·t + 1`, `gol_store.read_frame`), read in order by `book_chapters.ages.lifelines`: every agent's `ages` entry gives its birth iteration (the frame's iteration minus its age), and the last frame it is in its last iteration alive.

1. For each world and stretch of 25 birth iterations with at least 20 births, the Kaplan–Meier curve S(L) of their lives.
2. Left: Σ S(L) for L = 1 … 100. Right: the largest L with S(L) > ½.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py ages`.

hazard.title: The risk of dying, by age
hazard.caption: At each age a: of the agents alive after the game at age a − 1, the share that is gone after the game at age a — the agent's chance of dying at that age, pooled over the worlds, for agents born early in a world's life (orange) and in its settled life (blue). An age is drawn only where at least 200 agents reached it.
hazard.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames after every game (frame `2·t + 1`, `gol_store.read_frame`), read in order by `book_chapters.ages.lifelines`: every agent's `ages` entry gives its birth iteration (the frame's iteration minus its age), and the last frame it is in its last iteration alive.

1. For agents born in the period, with d − b + 1 iterations lived: at each L, the lives still going at L (lasting at least L) and those ending at L (lasting exactly L, not still going at the end).
2. Divide the second by the first (`book_chapters.ages.hazard`).

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py ages`.

wealth-age.title: Who the old are
wealth-age.caption: Every 25 iterations, the agents alive after the game in each age class: their mean tokens (left) and mean number of connections (right); each line is the median over the 30 worlds of the class's mean.
wealth-age.recipe:

two-sizes.title: Ages in worlds of two sizes
two-sizes.caption: The median age and the oldest agent after every game, in the 30 worlds of 100,000 tokens (blue, 1,500 iterations) and in the 30 worlds of 10,000 tokens of the first edition, Experiment 2 (yellow, 3,000 iterations). The line is the median of the worlds at each iteration, the darker band holds the middle half of them (from the 25th to the 75th percentile) and the paler band nine in ten (5th to 95th); a world that died is no longer counted.
two-sizes.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)).
